title: NMF cd solver: arrays passed to the Cython _update_cdnmf_fast must be made C-contiguous explicitly
answers: NMF fit_transform raises ValueError: ndarray is not C-contiguous
NMF breaks with new scipy version / scipy dev
body:
Symptom: `NMF(n_components=5).fit_transform(X)` (default solver="cd", nndsvd-style init) crashes with `ValueError: ndarray is not C-contiguous` from `_cdnmf_fast._update_cdnmf_fast`, seen with SciPy dev.
Root cause: `sklearn/decomposition/_cdnmf_fast.pyx:_update_cdnmf_fast` declares `W` as a `floating[:, ::1]` (C-contiguous) memoryview, but `sklearn/decomposition/_nmf.py:_fit_coordinate_descent` only forced `Ht` to C order. W from the SVD-based init inherits the memory layout of `scipy.linalg.svd` output, and SciPy changed its C/F ordering (scipy/scipy#24538).
Fix pattern: at the Python/Cython boundary, call `np.ascontiguousarray` on every array that the Cython signature declares `::1` (here both `W` and `Ht = H.T`). Don't rely on the layout an upstream library returns. Sparse X is converted csc->csr only when `sp.issparse(X) and X.format == "csc"`.
Constraints: this applies to any Cython kernel with `[:, ::1]` memoryviews. Transposes (`H.T`) and SVD outputs are the usual sources of F-ordered arrays. `sklearn/decomposition/tests/test_nmf.py:test_nmf_smoke` covers every init (None, nndsvd, nndsvda, nndsvdar, random) × solver (cd, mu) × tall/wide shape. Extend it when you add an init or solver, because the original bug was not caught by CI.
applies: sklearn/decomposition NMF coordinate-descent solver and other Python wrappers that call Cython kernels with C-contiguous memoryviews
